newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli labour ministry warns of strike surge.
newsitem.headline: Israeli labour ministry warns of strike surge.

text.p: Israel's labour ministry predicted on Tuesday that the Israeli economy would experience a sharp increase in strikes in 1997.

"The trend towards industrial quiet that characterised 1995 and most of 1996, leading to a reduction in the number of strikes, strikers and working days lost, has started to reverse itself," the ministry said, citing a report on labour relations in 1995.
"There are increasing signs of more labour disputes during 1997," it said.

The survey said plans by the government for wide-scale privatisation would prompt workers to take action for fear of firings at state-owned companies. The ministry also pointed to a growing tendency on the part of employers to cancel collective wage agreements as a key factor in labour unrest.
The report comes as the ministerial privatisation committee meets on Wednesday evening to discuss a plan prepared by officials for selling state-owned companies.
"This should worry three main elements in the economy: the government, Histadrut (trade union federation) and the employers," the study said.
It noted that five collective agreements were cancelled in 1994 and seven in 1995, but that 12 were annulled by employers last year.

With 1,000 such agreements registered with the ministry annually, "the absolute number of cancelled accords is not large but the increase in the rate of cancellation points to a trend," the survey said.
The ministry said there were 71 full-blown strikes in 1995, involving 75,792 workers compared with 75 strikes in 1994 in which 106,047 workers took part. It did not release any figures for 1996.
The Israeli economy lost 257,796 working days due to labour actions in 1995 against 729,553 days in 1994, a decline of 65 percent.
